'''Dejounte Murray''' (born September 19, 1996) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington Huskies]], and earned second-team all-conference honors in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12]] as a freshman in 2015–16.

Murray attended [[Rainier Beach High School]] in [[Rainier Beach, Seattle|Rainier Beach, Seattle, Washington]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.seattletimes.com/sports/uw-husky-basketball/dejounte-murray-already-trying-to-help-lead-the-way-for-uw-mens-basketball/|title=Dejounte Murray already trying to help lead the way for UW men’s basketball|date=14 July 2015|work=The Seattle Times|accessdate=22 April 2016}}</ref>

As a freshman at the [[University of Washington]], Murray was named second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] after averaged 16.1 points, 4.4 assists and  6.0 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite press release|title=2015-16 Pac-12 Men's Basketball All-Conference Honors|date=March 7, 2016|publisher=Pac-12|url=http://pac-12.com/article/2016/03/07/2015-16-pac-12-mens-basketball-all-conference-honors}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.seattletimes.com/sports/uw-husky-basketball/dejounte-murray-signs-with-lebron-james-agency-agent-rich-paul/|title=UW Huskies’ Dejounte Murray signs with LeBron James’ agency, agent Rich Paul|date=29 March 2016|work=The Seattle Times|accessdate=22 April 2016}}</ref> After the season, he entered the [[2016 NBA Draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/15054665/marquese-chriss-dejounte-murray-washington-huskies-declaring-nba-draft|title=Marquese Chriss, Dejounte Murray of Washington Huskies declaring for NBA draft|work=ESPN.com|accessdate=22 April 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.seattletimes.com/sports/uw-husky-basketball/washingtons-dejounte-murray-and-marquese-chriss-declare-for-nba-draft/|title=Washington’s Dejounte Murray and Marquese Chriss declare for NBA draft|date=23 March 2016|work=The Seattle Times|accessdate=22 April 2016}}</ref> Murray would be one of 19 players that year to receive special invitations to enter the draft live and in person. He'd also be a part of a record-high five different invitees to get their invitations after the original listing was unveiled to the public.
